transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. The proposal before us is a collateral analytics platform for the secured-lending business — vendor-hosted, priced at $2.7 million. It would handle collateral valuations and exception reports used by both credit and treasury. Before I record any decision, I'd like to follow our normal review process. FP&A and internal audit — do you have any relevant updates we should be aware of?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed the investment model this morning. I received the negotiated implementation quote, and a bank-controlled deployment costs exactly $3,200,000 all-in. The project does meet the committee's return hurdle at that amount. However, I should note that the revised quote has not yet been attached to the capital request, so the committee is currently seeing the $2.7 million vendor-hosted figure.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an important update from internal audit. While reviewing the control design this week, I found that collateral data must remain in a bank-controlled environment rather than the vendor's hosted environment. Internal audit also requires an independent access certification before go-live and monthly exception reviews for the first 6 months. None of these requirements have been added to the project file yet. This is directly relevant to the deployment model being discussed — the vendor-hosted approach as currently proposed would not satisfy our control requirements.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: The revised $3.2M bank-controlled deployment quote must be attached to the capital request before funds are disbursed.
Collateral data must reside in a bank-controlled environment; the vendor-hosted model is not approved.
An independent access certification must be completed before go-live.
Monthly exception reviews must be conducted for the first 6 months post go-live.
